entries.purpose: Protect a stored member or administrator password against an attacker who reads the database
entries.storageBoundary: The instance database, in user_account.password_hash. The salt and the parameters travel inside the encoding; there is no separate key.
entries.permittedUse: Verifying a sign-in and re-encoding a stored hash that sits below the current parameters. Never for a digest, an identifier or a signature.
entries.rotation: Raising a parameter is the rotation. A stored hash below the current parameters is re-encoded on its owner's next successful sign-in; storing that is best effort, so a database failure leaves the old hash in place rather than failing the login.
entries.revocation: Issuing a new credential replaces the hash and ends every session of the account.
entries.recovery: None is possible or needed: a hash is not recoverable by design, and a member who cannot sign in is given a new credential.
entries.retirement: Argon2id is replaced by encoding new and re-encoded passwords under the successor while the old encoding stays verifiable, which is what the re-encode path already does for a parameter change.

entries.purpose: The one-time password an instance mails a member for their first sign-in
entries.storageBoundary: Generated in memory, mailed to the member, and kept only as its Argon2id hash. The plaintext is never written to the database, a log or an administrative screen.
entries.permittedUse: One sign-in, after which the account must set a permanent password. It cannot become that permanent password.
entries.rotation: Issuing a credential again replaces the previous one and ends every session of the account.
entries.revocation: Withdrawing an unused credential clears the hash and its deadline.
entries.recovery: None: a lost credential is reissued, never recovered.
entries.retirement: Retired with the account, whose deactivation ends its sessions.

entries.purpose: Give an account with no credential a hash that no input can match, so an absent password is not an empty one
entries.storageBoundary: In memory only. The value is discarded after encoding; nothing ever needs to reproduce it.
entries.permittedUse: Standing in for a credential that does not exist. It is never sent, shown or verified against a member's input successfully.
entries.rotation: Not applicable: a new value is generated whenever one is needed.
entries.recovery: None is possible, which is the point.
entries.retirement: Replaced with the password hashing entry it shares an algorithm with.

entries.purpose: Count failed sign-ins per username and per address without keeping either in the counter
entries.storageBoundary: In-memory counters for the lifetime of the process. No key, and nothing written down.
entries.permittedUse: Grouping attempts. The digest is not an authenticator and proves nothing about who made an attempt.
entries.rotation: Not applicable: no key exists, and the counters do not outlive the process.
entries.recovery: None is needed; the counters rebuild themselves.
entries.retirement: A successor digest may replace it without migration, because nothing persists.

entries.purpose: Recognise a repeated booking request so a retry does not create a second booking
entries.storageBoundary: The instance database, beside the booking it identifies.
entries.permittedUse: Comparing one request to another. It carries no security claim and protects nothing.
entries.recovery: None is needed; a lost fingerprint costs at most a duplicate refusal.
entries.retirement: Replaceable with any digest, since nothing outside the instance reads it.

entries.purpose: Name the stored club logo so a browser can be told whether its copy is current
entries.storageBoundary: The instance database, and the ETag it becomes.
entries.permittedUse: Cache validation. It is not an integrity guarantee against a party that can write the row.
entries.recovery: None is needed; it is recomputed from the image.
entries.retirement: Replaceable with any digest; a changed algorithm invalidates caches once.

entries.purpose: Match an imported row against a person already on the roster
entries.storageBoundary: The instance database, on the imported reference.
entries.permittedUse: Deduplicating an import. It is not a pseudonym that may be published, because the input space of a name and a birth date is small enough to search.
entries.recovery: None is needed; it is recomputed from the roster.
entries.retirement: A change re-matches every stored reference, so it is made with an import run rather than in place.

entries.purpose: Name the seeded assessment dataset so a report says which data it was produced against
entries.storageBoundary: Computed at runtime from a constant in the image; nothing is stored.
entries.permittedUse: Identifying a dataset in a report.
entries.recovery: None is needed; it is recomputed.

entries.purpose: Give a submitted booking a client-side identity so a retry is recognised
entries.storageBoundary: The browser, for the life of one submission.
entries.permittedUse: Identifying a request. It authenticates nothing, which is why the non-secure-context fallback is acceptable.
entries.rotation: Not applicable: every submission generates one.

entries.purpose: Name an artefact, a configuration or a report the verification harness produced, so two runs can be compared
entries.storageBoundary: Build output and workflow artefacts. Nothing reaches an instance.
entries.permittedUse: Comparing and naming artefacts. No harness digest is a security control, and none is presented as evidence that content was not tampered with by a party who could write it.
entries.recovery: None is needed; a rerun recomputes everything.

entries.purpose: Give a test run values nothing else uses, such as a scratch database name or a throwaway password
entries.storageBoundary: The lifetime of one verification run. Nothing is written to a tracked file and nothing reaches an instance.
entries.permittedUse: Test fixtures only. No harness value ever becomes an operational credential.
entries.rotation: Not applicable: every run generates its own.

entries.purpose: Let anybody verify that a published image was built by this repository's release workflow
entries.storageBoundary: No long-lived private key exists. Sigstore issues a short-lived certificate against the workflow's OIDC identity and records the signature in a public transparency log.
entries.permittedUse: Signing a published image and its attestations. It says which workflow built the image, not that the image is free of defects.
entries.rotation: Every signing operation obtains a new short-lived certificate; there is nothing to rotate on a schedule.
entries.revocation: Not applicable to a keyless signature. A withdrawn release is deleted and stated as withdrawn.
entries.recovery: None is possible or needed: no material can be lost, and a signature can be produced again by re-running the release.
entries.retirement: Replaced by changing the signing action, which changes what a verifier is told to expect.

entries.purpose: Encrypt the protected part of a security assessment so only its custodian can read it
entries.storageBoundary: The recipient certificate is tracked; its expected fingerprint lives in a GitHub repository variable outside commit history, and the private key never enters this repository. The operational record is .github/security-evidence-key.json, which holds the custodian role and the decrypt-canary window and deliberately no second copy of the fingerprint.
entries.permittedUse: Sealing assessment evidence for its custodian. It is not a general-purpose encryption facility and no instance data passes through it.
entries.rotation: Replacing the recipient certificate means replacing the tracked certificate and the repository variable, which are separately held on purpose: changing only one blocks sealing rather than sealing to the wrong recipient.
entries.revocation: Removing the repository variable blocks sealing at the next run.
entries.recovery: A lost private key makes existing envelopes unreadable and cannot be recovered. That is bounded by the decrypt canary, which proves the key is still usable within its recorded window; a canary that cannot be verified is the signal to reseal under a new recipient.
entries.retirement: A successor recipient is introduced by sealing to it and letting the canary window of the previous one lapse.

entries.purpose: Encrypt and authenticate what a member's browser sends to the instance
entries.storageBoundary: The reverse proxy's own storage in the reference deployment. Courtside neither issues nor holds the material.
entries.permittedUse: The public entry point. Courtside does not ship a certificate authority and does not generate production key material.
entries.rotation: The proxy obtains and renews certificates itself; an operator supplying their own owns the renewal.
entries.revocation: The issuing authority's, and the operator's to request.
entries.recovery: A lost certificate is reissued by the authority; nothing in Courtside needs to be recovered with it.
entries.retirement: Follows what the proxy supports; Courtside states no cipher list of its own.

entries.purpose: Authenticate the mail relay an instance hands its outgoing messages to
entries.storageBoundary: The relay's certificate, read by the instance. No private material belongs to Courtside.
entries.permittedUse: Verifying the relay. Trusting an unverified relay certificate is a deliberate, separately named setting rather than a silent fallback.
entries.rotation: The relay's own renewal, which the instance observes rather than performs; a certificate whose remaining life falls below the configured share is reported.
entries.recovery: A relay that cannot present a usable certificate refuses the connection, and the message stays queued for retry rather than being sent in the clear.

entries.purpose: Sign outgoing mail so a receiving server can tell it came from the club's domain
entries.storageBoundary: The mail container's volume in the reference deployment. The public half is a DNS record the operator publishes.
entries.permittedUse: Signing the club's own outgoing mail.
entries.rotation: The operator publishes a new selector, signs under it, and retires the old record once nothing in flight relies on it.
entries.revocation: Removing the DNS record for a selector.
entries.recovery: A lost key is replaced by generating a new one under a new selector; no past message needs to be recoverable.
entries.retirement: The selector's DNS record is withdrawn after the change has propagated.
